knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-f752a3f56b14a01c14cc3a72.png)

Find the point on the line $y=-\frac{3}{2}x+1$ that is closest to the point $(-7,5)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(-7,5)$.

The given line has slope $-\frac{3}{2}$, so the perpendicular slope is $\frac{2}{3}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(5)&=\frac{2}{3}\left(x-(-7)\right) \\ y&=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{14}{3}+(5) \\ y&=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{29}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=-\frac{3}{2}x+1 \\ y &=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{29}{3}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}x+1&=\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{29}{3} \\ \left(-\frac{3}{2}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\right)x&=\frac{29}{3}-(1) \\ -\frac{13}{6}x&=\frac{26}{3} \\ x&=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=-\frac{3}{2}\left(-4\right)+(1) \\ y&=6+(1) \\ y&=7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $y=-\frac{3}{2}x+1$ closest to $(-7,5)$ is $(-4,7)$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-dd0a2f99a7d9a82e7ab4b96b.png)

Find the point on the line $y=\frac{3}{2}x-2$ that is closest to the point $(5,-1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(5,-1)$.

The given line has slope $\frac{3}{2}$, so the perpendicular slope is $-\frac{2}{3}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(-1)&=-\frac{2}{3}\left(x-(5)\right) \\ y&=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{10}{3}+(-1) \\ y&=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=\frac{3}{2}x-2 \\ y &=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}x-2&=-\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{7}{3} \\ \left(\frac{3}{2}-\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\right)x&=\frac{7}{3}-(-2) \\ \frac{13}{6}x&=\frac{13}{3} \\ x&=2\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{3}{2}\left(2\right)+(-2) \\ y&=3+(-2) \\ y&=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $y=\frac{3}{2}x-2$ closest to $(5,-1)$ is $(2,1)$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-cd403fe0b5fcb340d605e8b1.png)

Find the point on the line $y=-2x-2$ that is closest to the point $(-4,1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(-4,1)$.

The given line has slope $-2$, so the perpendicular slope is $\frac{1}{2}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(1)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-(-4)\right) \\ y&=\frac{1}{2}x+2+(1) \\ y&=\frac{1}{2}x+3\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=-2x-2 \\ y &=\frac{1}{2}x+3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-2&=\frac{1}{2}x+3 \\ \left(-2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)x&=3-(-2) \\ -\frac{5}{2}x&=5 \\ x&=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=-2\left(-2\right)+(-2) \\ y&=4+(-2) \\ y&=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $y=-2x-2$ closest to $(-4,1)$ is $(-2,2)$.
